name: Why do hairline drywall cracks repeatedly appear around kitchen doorframes in the Denver area?

mainEntity.name: Why do hairline drywall cracks repeatedly appear around kitchen doorframes in the Denver area?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homes across the Denver metro area, including Aurora, Centennial, and Parker, frequently experience soil-driven foundation movement due to expansive bentonite clay. When expansive soils expand during wet seasons and shrink during dry spells, home framing shifts slightly, producing diagonal drywall cracks around kitchen doorways, pass-throughs, and ceiling corners. Additionally, Colorado's semi-arid climate and low indoor winter humidity dry out wood studs and joint compound, making older tape seams brittle. A repair contractor assesses whether cracks stem from seasonal settlement, structural movement, or local moisture before taping with flexible fiberglass or paper mesh and applying compound.
acceptedAnswer.description: Denver's expansive clay soils cause minor foundation shifts that stress framing around wall openings, while low indoor humidity dries out joint compound, causing hairline cracks to reappear.
